name: The Mommyheads
label: Simple Machines
lede: Adam Cohen started the Mommyheads in 1987, still in high school in New York. A decade later Geffen signed them, barely marketed the record and let them go; they reunited in 2008 and have been releasing records ever since.

eras.title: Two records made in high school
eras.text: Adam Cohen was a student at New York's High School of Music and Art when he formed the band. Wharton Tiers, who worked with Sonic Youth, recorded the first EP, and Fang Records put out the first album.

yt: Adam Elk on the band's beginnings
years.h: Adam Cohen starts the Mommyheads while still in high school
years.p: Cohen, a student at New York's High School of Music and Art, forms the band in 1987 with drummer [[Jan Kotik|4a251c11-a62e-4e29-a578-c745532b1799]] and bassist Matt Patrick, according to AllMusic.
years.xp: Wikipedia's account of the first line-up also lists Jude Reveley on guitar and dulcimer and Tom Kotik on bass and guitar. Both early records were made while the members were still in high school.

years.h: Wharton Tiers, Sonic Youth's engineer, cuts the Magumbo Meatpie EP
years.p: Four songs, recorded late in 1987 and released on Sit and Spin, a label Wikipedia describes as run out of an NYU dorm. Three of them resurface on Fang's Antipop: New York Underground Mix compilation.
years.xp: Wikipedia calls the EP extremely rare now. Tiers had worked with [[Sonic Youth|5cbef01b-cc35-4f52-af7b-d0df0c4f61b9]], and AllMusic says the record made a favorable impression on downtown audiences.

years.h: A producer who cites Pussy Galore and James Brown makes Acorn
years.p: The full-length debut comes out on Fang Records, with Cohen, Kotik and Patrick. Producer Chris Rael of Church of Betty names XTC, James Brown and Pussy Galore in the liner notes.

eras.title: Moving west under a new name
eras.text: Adam Cohen becomes Adam Elk and moves to San Francisco. Michael Holt and Dan Fisherman, both from the New York band the Connotations, replace Jan Kotik, and the band's first records for Simple Machines follow.

years.h: Cohen becomes Elk and the band moves to San Francisco
years.p: Wikipedia says he changed his name to avoid confusion with Leonard Cohen's musician son. Keyboardist Michael Holt and drummer Dan Fisherman, both from the Connotations, come in, and Kotik is out.
years.xp:
Elk, Holt and Fisherman have anchored the band ever since, through the 1998 split and the 2008 reunion.

Kotik stays in the story: a tribute show for him is what brings the band back together.

years.h: Seventeen home demos land on Simple Machines
years.p: Swiss Army Knife collects Adam Elk's four-track recordings and comes out on Simple Machines, the Arlington, Virginia label run by [[Jenny Toomey|246fc8dd-a667-4a5b-868a-a5897bcd6c59]] and Kristin Thomson. Four songs get re-recorded for later albums.

years.big: "It was the closest thing to looking at those horrible pictures of yourself in high school before shoving them back into the attic."
years.h: Coming Into Beauty is cut in two cities with two line-ups
years.p: Elk on the original release. Sessions ran at 6/8 Studios in New York and Cloud 9 in Chico, California, with Elk, Holt, Fisherman and Matt Patrick; Elk and Patrick wrote most of it.
years.xp: Glide says the album went out of print and offline for nearly three decades. Glide's description: "a gently kaleidoscopic patchwork." Its writer says the musicians were "just shy of their 20s" and recorded whenever and wherever they could.

eras.title: Two small-label records that reach Don Was
eras.text: Bassist Jeff Palmer, late of Sister Double Happiness, replaces Matt Patrick. The line-up makes Flying Suit and Bingham's Hole, and the second one finds its way to Don Was.

years.h: Jeff Palmer takes the bass from Matt Patrick
years.p: Palmer arrives from SST's Sister Double Happiness in time for Flying Suit. Wikipedia dates Patrick's tenure as 1987 to 1993.

yt: Live at Midtown Music Hall, Nov 16, 1994
years.h: Flying Suit is the first record with Palmer on bass
years.p: Out on Dromedary Records, with songwriting now led by Elk and the odd song from Holt.
years.xp: Wikipedia's description of the live shows from this period includes "a fetid, bongwater-soaked towel." Fan video survives of a set at Midtown Music Hall on November 16, 1994.

years.h: Don Was hears Bingham's Hole
years.p: Out on Dot Dot Dash and produced by Peter Katis, it's the last independent full-length and adds funk and boogie. It reaches Was, who will produce the next one.
years.xp: Katis went on to work with bands like The National. AllMusic says the record found its way to Was, who helped the band land its Geffen deal.

eras.title: Geffen, briefly
eras.text: Was helps them land a Geffen deal and co-produces a big, Beatles-minded record. Geffen barely markets it, and by early 1998 the band is done.

q: Postgraduate students of the Beach Boys and the Beatles.
Jon Pareles, The New York Times
yt: Jaded, live at the Tin Angel, Philadelphia, 1997
years.h: Tower of Power's horns turn up on the Geffen album
years.p: Don Was co-produces The Mommyheads with the band at Ocean Way and at his home studio. The horn section plays on Wake Up Irene, and [[Jon Brion|a32e4aac-1db8-4dc6-be34-a813c4530627]] plays Chamberlin on Screwed and Thought of You.
years.xp:
Jim Scott mixed it, and Jaded was the first single. The record earned a Bammie nomination in 1997, and Geffen gave it minimal marketing support.

The Contra Costa Times heard "the spirit of the Abbey Road-era Beatles" gliding in and out. The band toured North America behind it anyway.

years.h: Geffen lets them go, and a San Francisco show is the last
years.p: Wikipedia says the label drops the band in a restructuring. The band plays a final show in San Francisco and calls it quits.
years.xp: Many fans came to read it as a cautionary tale of a major label "ruining" a band, according to Wikipedia. AllMusic says Geffen more or less abandoned the album.

eras.title: A tribute show, and the band is back
eras.text: Original drummer Jan Kotik dies in December 2007, and a tribute show in New York pulls the old line-up back together. The reunion sticks.

years.h: Jan Kotik, the first drummer, dies of cancer
years.p: [[Jan Kotik|4a251c11-a62e-4e29-a578-c745532b1799]] dies on December 13, 2007, after a three-year fight with cancer. His old bandmates book a tribute show in New York.

years.h: A tribute show for Kotik turns into a reunion
years.p: Elk, Holt and Fisherman play the New York tribute, with Jeff Palmer on bass, and decide to keep going. You're Not a Dream follows that year on Bladen County Records.
years.xp: In the decade before, Elk had released the solo album Labello and become a composer for TV commercials. Palmer had joined Sub Pop's [[Sunny Day Real Estate|86b24e8f-a4d9-4c84-83ee-fde0d14ad9fa]] and Holt had made solo records. Fisherman was working as a computer programmer and teaching math and philosophy at the Randolph School in Wappingers Falls, New York.

years.h: You're Not a Dream: the first record since Geffen
years.p: The comeback album opens a second act that turns out to be prolific.

yt: Jaded, live at Polar Studios, Sweden, May 2010
years.h: Sweden had been listening the whole time they were gone
years.p: AllMusic says the catalog found an unexpectedly passionate audience in Scandinavia, and the reunited band becomes a perennial touring act there. Dromedary's Finest Specimens arrives October 19.
years.xp: The retrospective gathers cuts from most of the studio albums plus unreleased live tracks, demos and one new song. A live version of Jaded from a Polar Studios session in Sweden, May 2010, is on video.

years.h: Jason McNair arrives on bass and stays
years.p: McNair replaces Jeff Palmer in 2010 and holds the job through the later records, according to Wikipedia.

eras.title: An album nearly every year
eras.text: After Delicate Friction, Vulnerable Boy, Soundtrack to the World's End (2018) and Future You (2019), AllMusic says the band starts putting out a new LP every year from 2020. They tour Sweden and the US, and in 2024 one reaches No. 10 on college radio.

years.h: Delicate Friction brings new songs, then Vulnerable Boy
years.p: Wikipedia calls Delicate Friction their first all-new record since the mid-1990s. Vulnerable Boy follows in 2012 on Dromedary and Dead Frog.

years.h: The Geffen album comes back, 23 years on
years.p: The 1997 self-titled album is reissued and becomes the 14th most-added LP on college radio in mid-February 2020. Big Takeover calls it "their masterpiece."
years.xp: The band also puts out a new record that year, New Kings of Pop, which reaches No. 58 on college radio and No. 16 on Sub Modern in October. TakeEffect Magazine's verdict: "safe to say that The Mommyheads are at a creative high."

years.src: Glide Magazine · Stratton's Setlist · Wikipedia: Mommyheads
years.h: Coming Into Beauty returns after nearly three decades offline
years.p: Fred Kavorkian remasters the 1992 Simple Machines album at Avatar Studios, with new cover art by Marc Stromberg. The digital release is February 12, 2021.
years.xp:
Glide's verdict: "the most potent document of the Mommyheads at their most unhinged and daring." The remaster was the 12th most-added record on college radio the week of February 16 and peaked at No. 67.

Elk, on commissioning new artwork: "It was such a relief." On the remaster: "like asking Fred to sonically climb a mountain for us." The Bandcamp deluxe edition adds four bonus tracks from the original digital audio tape sessions.

yt: TV Dinner, live at Melody Box, Stockholm, Sept 2, 2021
years.h: Age of Isolation gives them a No. 29 on college radio
years.p: Wikipedia cites it as their highest college-radio ranking to that point. The album comes out in September.
years.xp: Critic Bill Kopp wrote that, more than thirty years after their debut, the band was "making some of the best music of their career." The clip is from Melody Box in Stockholm, September 2, 2021.

yt: Adam Elk on the band's long history and Coney Island Kid
years.h: A concept album sends the band back to 1970s Brooklyn
years.p: Coney Island Kid is set in the Brooklyn Elk grew up in. The band tours Sweden and the US in early September, with several sold-out shows.
years.xp: AllMusic counts it as the band's 15th album. Elk was born in Brooklyn, and the record looks at the borough in the '70s. AllMusic also notes that multi-instrumentalist Jackie Simons has joined the group.

years.h: One Eyed Band reaches No. 10 on college radio, their peak
years.p: Wikipedia calls it a career high. It lands on several year-end top 10 lists, and No Quietus follows on November 7, 2025.
years.xp: The album comes out in late November 2024, after a West Coast tour in October. No Quietus reaches No. 38 on college radio and No. 17 on Sub Modern in December. Wikipedia lists Super Emotional Intelligence for 2027.
